bull.b: Rapid growth in branded ophthalmic revenue indicates expanding product adoption and commercial execution across the portfolio. The mix also supports a more scalable business model, while continued prescription and product demand can provide a durable foundation for revenue growth over the next several quarters.

Strong VEVYE prescription growth combined with broader payer coverage improves access to the product and expands its addressable patient base. Rising covered prescriptions can support sustained demand, improve commercial productivity, and strengthen Harrow's position in the ophthalmic market.

Adding an established dry-eye product and an experienced commercial team broadens Harrow's ophthalmic portfolio and increases its reach with eye-care practices. Integration with existing infrastructure may create cross-selling opportunities and adds a defined source of future revenue growth.

bear.b: The combination of rising debt and sharply reduced equity leaves Harrow with limited balance-sheet flexibility. High leverage can constrain investment in product development and commercialization, while increasing the importance of sustained earnings and cash generation to support financial obligations.

The reversal from strong positive cash generation in 2025 to negative operating and free cash flow in the latest period signals uneven self-funding capacity. Persistent volatility could increase reliance on financing or other capital sources while the company continues expanding its product platform.

The sharp reduction in adjusted EBITDA expectations shows that revenue growth is not yet translating consistently into planned earnings. Lower gross margins, development spending, filing costs, and integration expenses may continue to limit operating leverage and delay more durable profitability.
